primary_claim: Simple unsupervised elicitation baselines combining random-label few-shot prompting, bootstrapping, and enforced logical consistency recover 83-100% of the accuracy gap between zero-shot and golden-label many-shot prompting (and 91-99% of the gap for fine-tuning) on Wen et al.'s ICM benchmark datasets, nearly matching the full ICM algorithm, but this advantage largely disappears when the training set size is increased from ~2k to ~30k examples.

effect.metric: % of zero-shot-to-golden-label accuracy gap recovered (few-shot / fine-tuning)
effect.value: random-label few-shot alone: 53-93% (few-shot) / 62-96% (fine-tuning); combined bootstrap+consistency method: 83-100% (few-shot) / 91-99% (fine-tuning), across GSM8K, Alpaca, TruthfulQA, Gender datasets

contradicts_or_qualifies: Reports difficulty reproducing Wen et al.'s ICM results using the official repo: label accuracy collapsed during training (e.g. Alpaca rose to ~75% then collapsed to ~46% before labelling the full batch), and identifies a prompt-formatting issue (a trailing space) in the ICM repo's prompts that may have harmed its reported performance.
stated_future_work: Explore more challenging and adversarial datasets to evaluate unsupervised elicitation methods, since simple techniques already close most of the gap on datasets like Alpaca and GSM8K
Release an upcoming paper applying bootstrapping and other unsupervised elicitation methods in more realistic settings, where they find these methods perform significantly worse
limitations_stated: There is no strong reason to expect these simple techniques to elicit superhuman knowledge from very powerful base models, since they may fail where salient human beliefs are wrong
The advantage of simple unsupervised methods over golden fine-tuning shrinks or disappears when the training set size is increased from ~2k to ~30k examples
TruthfulQA's consistency-enforcement scheme can leak information and artificially boost accuracy (Appendix C)
ICM was computationally prohibitive to reproduce (O(n^2) forward passes) and reproduction attempts using the official repo showed accuracy collapsing during training
All reported results are under idealized conditions: approximately balanced training sets, no salient competing features, and an objective ground-truth label for every example
quote: A simple method which combines these recovers 83–100% of the gap between zero-shot accuracy and many-shot prompting with golden labels, and iterative fine-tuning with this method recovers 91–99% of the gap between untrained models and golden fine-tuned models.
